note: Generic, per-tier housing/farming-system photos, reused across every brand assigned that tier. Real photo sourced first per housing-imagery.md's process; AI generation only as a last resort when no genuinely free, clearly-licensed real photo existed. Policy revised 2026-07-31 (founder directive): an unmodified, undramatized real photo of an actual documented facility is fine to use as a tier illustration, including when the source is advocacy-sourced or the facility is identifiable -- the app never discloses or claims which company's facility is shown (every tier photo carries the same generic 'similar to this' caption regardless of source), so showing a real, accurate, unmanipulated photo is not a misrepresentation. What's still required: the photo must not be manipulated/staged to look worse than reality, and must not depict active distress/injury/gore -- ordinary documentary content only.

gestation-crate.jpg.license: CC BY 3.0 (explicit release confirmed via Wikimedia's permissions process)
gestation-crate.jpg.author: Humane Society of the United States, photographed November 2010
gestation-crate.jpg.depicts: Smithfield Foods/Murphy Brown gestation-crate barn, Waverly, Virginia. Superseded an earlier AI-generated placeholder (2026-07-31) after founder review: unmodified, undramatized real documentation of an actual, verified industry practice (Smithfield's own sourcing data already confirms crate use) is preferable to a synthetic stand-in, as long as the app never claims this specific photo depicts any OTHER company's facility -- it's shown with the same generic 'similar to this' caption every tier photo uses, never captioned as 'Smithfield's facility.' Reviewed directly before use: bright natural lighting, no visible injury/blood, no dramatized framing -- an ordinary documentary shot despite the advocacy source.

wild-caught.jpg.author: C. Ortiz Rojas, NOAA
wild-caught.jpg.depicts: Commercial purse-seine catch (Chilean jack mackerel, not tuna specifically) -- illustrates the GENERIC wild-caught commercial fishing practice, not a species- or company-specific claim. All 3 tuna companies in the catalog (StarKist, Bumble Bee, Wild Planet) are wild-caught; no real, clearly-licensed, non-advocacy tuna-specific purse-seine photo was found in the time spent searching.
